validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE/tooling: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to every fetch attempt this run (confirmed via WebFetch and the MediaWiki raw/API endpoints), matching this run's scope note that the wiki-citation harvest failed for the whole batch, so I could not read what the sheet itself cites. The session's WebSearch tool was also already exhausted (200/200 budget used by other parallel subagents) before I could use it. I then tried ~10 alternative search surfaces via WebFetch as a substitute (Brave, DuckDuckGo html/lite, Bing, Ecosia, Startpage, Mojeek, Yandex, Qwant, searx.be, Marginalia): all returned CAPTCHA/403/429 blocks or irrelevant localized junk (Bing served French Outlook-forum results for an English query). Brave briefly worked once (returned a real Wikipedia hit for 'Gali Jagir' village) then 429'd for the remainder of the session and never recovered despite retries spaced minutes apart. SNGPL's and OGRA's own corporate sites were reachable but only expose aggregate transmission-system statistics (SNGPL's 'Transmission Network Map' page renders no text content via fetch; OGRA's site 403'd). No Wikipedia article on Dandot, Gali Jagir, Wah Cantonment, or Chakwal District mentions this pipeline. So no public, independently citable URL could be produced this session for this specific segment -- that is a tooling-access gap, not evidence of non-existence.

What DOES corroborate existence, independently of GEM: this batch's own GulfPub (Petroleum Economist PE World Map, source_tier=2, scraped 2025-12-11) reconciliation crosswalk -- staged at batches/pakistan-gas/staging/recon-gulfpub-20260807/canonical_records.json and surfaced in the delivered workbook batches/pakistan-gas/deliverables/pipelines_batch_20260807_1530_ET_pakistan-gas_reconciliation-gulfpub.xlsx (Gas_Overlaps tab) -- contains two GulfPub records that name-match, diameter-match, operator-match and status-match this exact row: 'Gali Jagir Line II' (CC1->Gali Jagir, 16in, ~120-126km, 300 MMcf/d, operator 'Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd') and 'Gali Jagir - Wah' (Gali Jagir->Wah, 16in, ~42km, 300 MMcf/d, same operator). GulfPub is scraped and ingested completely independently of GEM, so this is real independent corroboration even though it is not a public webpage I can cite as a [ref] URL (its recorded source_url field is only SNGPL's generic homepage, which I confirmed via url_verifier does NOT contain 'Gali Jagir' -- so I did not fabricate that as a citation). Combined GulfPub segment length for the analogous CC1->Gali Jagir->Wah path is ~167.4km vs GEM's 153.51km for Dandot->Gali Jagir->Wah -- a ~9% variance, plausibly explained by GulfPub's 'CC1' (likely a compressor-station node near Dandot, not the village itself) being a different exact start point than GEM's 'Dandot', not evidence of a different or nonexistent pipeline. Diameter (16in) and operator match exactly.

Second, general corroboration: Wikipedia's Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited article states that at SNGPL's founding it inherited two legacy systems, one being the 'Dhulian-Rawalpindi-Wah system: 82 miles (132 km) of 6 inches (150 mm) diameter pipeline' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sui_Northern_Gas_Pipelines_Limited, verified live and mentions 'Dhulian' and 'Wah'). This confirms a real, decades-old SNGPL transmission corridor running the Dhulian(Attock oilfield area)-Gali Jagir-Wah axis -- the same axis GulfPub's 'Dhulian - Gali Jagir' (10in) and 'Gali Jagir Line'/'Gali Jagir - Wah' segments trace -- which has clearly been progressively uprated from the original 6in line to today's parallel 10/16/30in lines as demand grew. I am not using this Wikipedia citation as a value-ref (its 6in/132km figures don't match this row's 16in/153.51km and it doesn't name Gali Jagir or Dandot specifically), only as context supporting that this is a genuine, long-standing corridor rather than a fabricated GEM-only entity.

DUPLICATE check vs the 63-pipeline roster: P4162 'Dandot-Gali Jagir-Wah Gas Pipeline II' (10in, 30in dia; 151.92km) is NOT a duplicate of P4161. GulfPub confirms these are two physically distinct parallel lines on the same corridor: P4161 corresponds to the single 16in GulfPub line (Gali Jagir Line II + Gali Jagir-Wah, both 16in), while P4162 corresponds to GulfPub's separate 30in 'Gali Jagir Line' plus 10in 'Dhulian - Gali Jagir' and 10in 'Gali Jagir - Wah' -- matching GEM's listed multi-value diameter '10, 30' for P4162 exactly. This mirrors the roster's other Roman-numeral loopline pairs (Sui-Multan Gas Pipeline/Loopline I/II/III, Sidhnai-Faisalabad Gas Pipeline/II) where 'I'/'II' denote parallel pipes of different vintage/diameter on the same route, not double-counted segments. No merge recommended.

CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is appropriate for a 153.51km SNGPL cross-district (Chakwal->Attock) trunk segment feeding the Wah industrial/cantonment area -- this is not a short field-gathering or distribution feeder line. Fuel=Gas is uncontested.

ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL) 100% is consistent with GulfPub's operator field on every matching record. Endpoints (StartLocation=Dandot, Chakwal, Punjab; EndLocation=Wah, Punjab) are geographically coherent -- Dandot and Gali Jagir and Wah are all real, verifiable Punjab locations (confirmed via Wikipedia/Brave for Gali Jagir village, Attock District) lying on a plausible SE-to-NW corridor, and GulfPub's coordinates for its 'Gali Jagir' and 'Wah' nodes are consistent with this routing.

SPEC: Diameter (16in) matches the independent GulfPub proxy exactly. Length (153.51km) is within ~9% of the closest independent two-segment proxy (~167.4km) -- a variance I attribute to differing start-point convention (CC1 vs Dandot) rather than a data error, but flagging it explicitly per the corroboration-tier rule since it is not an exact match. Capacity is blank in GEM; GulfPub's matching segments show 300 MMcf/d, but per instructions I am leaving Capacity blank rather than force-filling a value I could not independently verify with a citable public source this session.

Net: no existence, duplicate, classification, or attribution concern survives scrutiny -- the only caveats are (1) the ~9% length variance against an imperfect independent proxy, and (2) that no public, url_verifier-passing citation could be attached this pass purely due to this session's tooling outages (gem.wiki 403, WebSearch budget exhausted, every alternate search surface blocked/rate-limited). Recommend a follow-up ref-sweep pass on this row once normal search tooling is restored.
